thread.title: Macquarie Analysts Give Apple (AAPL) a $197.00 Price Target

author: Shane Hupp
title: Macquarie Analysts Give Apple (AAPL) a $197.00 Price Target
text:
Tweet
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) has been given a $197.00 target price by investment analysts at Macquarie in a research note issued on Monday. The brokerage currently has a “buy” rating on the iPhone maker’s stock. Macquarie’s target price would suggest a potential upside of 3.19% from the company’s current price.
AAPL has been the topic of several other reports. Barclays dropped their target price on Apple from $170.00 to $168.00 and set an “equal weight” rating on the stock in a report on Friday, March 16th. BidaskClub cut Apple from a “buy” rating to a “hold” rating in a research report on Friday. Morgan Stanley lowered their price objective on Apple from $203.00 to $200.00 and set an “overweight” rating for the company in a research report on Friday, April 20th. Bank of America reaffirmed a “buy” rating and set a $220.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research report on Friday, March 23rd. Finally, Vetr raised Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $184.49 price objective for the company in a research report on Monday, March 5th. One research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, seventeen have issued a hold rating, thirty-one have given a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the stock. Apple presently has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus target price of $205.87. Get Apple alerts:
AAPL stock traded down $0.79 during trading on Monday, reaching $190.91. 2,675,774 shares of the company traded hands, compared to its average volume of 20,100,268. Apple has a 12 month low of $142.20 and a 12 month high of $194.20. The company has a market cap of $972.69 billion, a P/E ratio of 20.73, a PEG ratio of 1.58 and a beta of 1.29. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80, a current ratio of 1.46 and a quick ratio of 1.37. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its quarterly earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 EPS for the quarter, beating analysts’ consensus estimates of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. The company had revenue of $61.14 billion during the quarter, compared to analysts’ expectations of $60.94 billion. During the same period last year, the business posted $2.10 earnings per share. The firm’s revenue was up 15.6% compared to the same quarter last year. analysts anticipate that Apple will post 11.42 EPS for the current year.
Apple announced that its board has authorized a share buyback program on Tuesday, May 1st that allows the company to buyback $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This buyback authorization allows the iPhone maker to purchase up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares buyback programs are generally a sign that the company’s board of directors believes its stock is undervalued.
In other Apple news, insider Luca Maestri sold 4,769 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Friday, June 1st. The shares were sold at an average price of $189.54, for a total transaction of $903,916.26. Following the sale, the insider now directly owns 68,044 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $12,897,059.76. The transaction was disclosed in a legal filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which is available at this hyperlink . Also, SVP Daniel J. Riccio sold 17,375 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction that occurred on Wednesday, April 4th. The stock was sold at an average price of $169.12, for a total transaction of $2,938,460.00. Following the sale, the senior vice president now directly owns 66,191 shares in the company, valued at $11,194,221.92. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders have sold a total of 256,853 shares of company stock worth $45,378,566 over the last three months. Insiders own 0.06% of the company’s stock.
A number of institutional investors and hedge funds have recently bought and sold shares of AAPL. Jarislowsky Fraser Ltd grew its stake in shares of Apple by 22.4% during the 3rd quarter. Jarislowsky Fraser Ltd now owns 22,515 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $3,470,000 after acquiring an additional 4,118 shares during the period. Fjarde AP Fonden Fourth Swedish National Pension Fund boosted its stake in shares of Apple by 1.7% in the third quarter. Fjarde AP Fonden Fourth Swedish National Pension Fund now owns 1,234,364 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $190,240,000 after acquiring an additional 20,689 shares during the last quarter. Shelton Capital Management boosted its stake in shares of Apple by 2.3% in the third quarter. Shelton Capital Management now owns 437,397 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $67,412,000 after acquiring an additional 9,758 shares during the last quarter. Hikari Power Ltd acquired a new stake in shares of Apple in the third quarter worth approximately $208,000. Finally, Oakmont Partners LLC boosted its stake in shares of Apple by 10.6% in the fourth quarter. Oakmont Partners LLC now owns 13,971 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $2,364,000 after acquiring an additional 1,335 shares during the last quarter. 58.13% of the stock is currently owned by hedge funds and other institutional investors.
